## New Features

- Added GPT-6 Sol and Luna, including Amazon Bedrock support and migration prompts for older models. (#47332, #47347)
- Enabled fullscreen transcripts by default and added Shift-click to extend text selections. (#47178, #47414)
- Enabled automatic background-server startup for eligible interactive sessions, with recovery choices when server settings are incompatible. (#47179, #47318)
- Added an `f` shortcut to fork conversations open in another app, preserving drafts and queued prompts. (#47185)
- Made `/import` available in remote sessions and local background-server sessions. (#47317)
- Improved terminal rendering with Unicode bullets, checkboxes, aligned equations, and optimization notation. (#47191, #47322)

## Bug Fixes

- Preserved active voice conversations when switching threads. (#47381)
- Recovered unsent question answers into the composer when turns end, without disrupting active history searches. (#47422, #47423)
- Respected tmux mouse settings and restored native scrollback for Terminal.app over SSH in automatic screen mode. (#47399, #47417)
- Fixed configured proxy routing for realtime connections and standalone web search, including search redirects. (#47101, #47142, #47204)
- Added retries for transient file-upload failures and increased the upload timeout to five minutes. (#47122, #47393)
- Enforced network restrictions across redirects and ongoing HTTP and WebSocket traffic, including cancellation when policy changes revoke access. (#47389, #47407)

prs.title: Support close-on-exec attachments without changing PTY semantics
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Support close-on-exec attachments without changing PTY semantics

## Why

Passing extra descriptors to a PTY previously selected behavior intended for inherited escalation sockets: no EOF on stdin close, different signal exit statuses, and no default `SHELL`. Launch attachments need ordinary PTY behavior and must survive execution even when marked `FD_CLOEXEC`.

## What changed

- Add `ChildFds::Attached` alongside `ChildFds::Inherited` to distinguish launch attachments from legacy inherited descriptors.
- Preserve ordinary EOF, default `SHELL`, and signal exit status behavior for PTY attachments.
- Allow explicitly supplied close-on-exec descriptors through pipe and PTY launches without changing the parent's descriptor flags, using child-side flag updates and macOS spawn inheritance actions.
- Update existing callers to use `ChildFds::Inherited`.

## Testing

Add Unix coverage for attachment accessibility, unchanged parent descriptor flags, default `SHELL`, and signal exit statuses. Extend the PTY stdin-draining test to cover attachments and EOF delivery.

prs.title: Enable terminal input approval by default
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Enable terminal input approval by default

## What changed

Promote `write_stdin_approval` to stable and enable it by default.

## Testing

Update the stdin approval suite to rely on the default feature setting. Adjust the background network approval test to account for terminal input review before network access and explicitly wait for the network assessment.

prs.title: Allow hosts to provide agent controllers through ThreadManager
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Allow hosts to provide agent controllers through ThreadManager

## What changed

- Add `ThreadManager::with_agent_control_factory` to select a host-owned controller asynchronously using the final thread ID for new and cold-resumed threads. Keep local control as the default, reuse live controllers on warm resume, and preserve parent controllers for internal sessions.
- Fail startup on factory errors or when a provided controller's identity does not match the session identity.
- Defer root service-tier updates to host controllers until thread registration succeeds, preventing failed starts from changing settings on a shared controller.

prs.title: Preserve explicit user goal updates in Guardian authorization
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve explicit user goal updates in Guardian authorization

## Why

Explicit user goal edits can restrict permitted actions, such as “Inspect only; do not publish.” Guardian needs these edits as authorization evidence even though they are recorded as contextual messages.

## What changed

- Add `UserGoalUpdate` and a recording API for objective, status, and clear updates without scheduling a model response.
- Use host annotations to retain goal updates in Guardian review history and root authorization evidence, and invalidate cached authorization when updates are recorded.
- Omit oversized objectives whole and mark their evidence incomplete so truncation cannot turn a restriction into a grant.
- Keep item injection from updating shared model and multi-agent metadata.

## Testing

Extend authorization, retained-context, and review snapshot tests to cover goal-edit cache invalidation, root goal visibility from child threads, and restrictive goals reaching Guardian alongside managed policies.

prs.title: Fix sleep interruption test event handling and fixture lifetime
Fix a lost wakeup in the unified exec termination test
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix a lost wakeup in the unified exec termination test

Use `notify_one()` instead of `notify_waiters()` in
`terminating_initial_exec_command_rechecks_initial_response_state` to retain
the release notification if the termination waiter has not registered yet.
This prevents the test from timing out due to a missed notification.

prs.title: Stabilize thread resume and memory dual-write tests
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Stabilize thread resume and memory dual-write tests

Wait for an assistant item to start before resuming a running paginated
thread, ensuring the user message has reached live history. Emit the initial
response events before the gate and keep completion gated during resume.

Increase the memory dual-write test's consolidation timeout from 10 to 60
seconds to allow Git workspace and agent process startup under contention
on Windows CI runners.

prs.title: Retry Guardian reviews when authorization changes
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Retry Guardian reviews when authorization changes

## Why

New user input during a Guardian review invalidated an in-flight approval and aborted the pending action, even when the input was only a status inquiry. Review the action again against the latest authorization evidence so it can proceed or be denied based on the updated instructions.

## What changed

- Treat stale authorization as a retryable review error within the existing attempt budget and shared deadline.
- Refresh authorization evidence for each attempt while keeping the pending action fixed, and record evidence from the completed attempt.
- Preserve cancellation and history-reset aborts, and deny approval if stale authorization exhausts the retry budget.

## Testing

Add and update coverage for parent status updates, authorization revocation, repeated updates, cancellation, history resets, and retry deadlines. Verify that refreshed reviews see the latest input and that the pending action executes exactly once only after approval.

Bind Guardian async scores to target environment permissions
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Bind Guardian async scores to target environment permissions

## Why

Asynchronous Guardian scoring omitted the target environment's denied-read restrictions, and cached score authorization did not include that permission context. A score from one environment could therefore be reused for an action in another environment with different restrictions.

## What changed

- Share permission resolution between synchronous review and asynchronous scoring, including resolving `write_stdin` targets from the owning terminal session.
- Include environment identity and denied-read paths/globs in async scoring context and cached score authorization.
- Fall back to synchronous review when permission evidence cannot be resolved or exceeds the async limit of 3,000 bytes, rather than omitting restrictions.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for rejecting cached scores with different environments or denied paths, passing the target environment's restrictions to the classifier, and rejecting oversized async permission evidence.

prs.title: Stabilize Rosetta test timing and retry delay telemetry
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Stabilize Rosetta test timing and retry delay telemetry

## Why

Cold Rosetta translation and cache invalidation from hard-linked executables can interfere with timed CLI tests. Sampling the clock twice also makes local retry telemetry report a delay shorter than the selected backoff.

## What changed

- Warm CLI fixtures with `--version` on macOS x86_64 before timed checks, and use copies or Unix symlinks to avoid invalidating the shared executable's Rosetta cache.
- Use one clock sample to calculate the response retry deadline and recorded delay.
- Include the retry telemetry event in delay-range assertion failures for the headerless rate-limit stream test.

prs.title: Keep the TUI responsive during clipboard copies
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Keep the TUI responsive during clipboard copies

## Why

Native clipboard setup and writes can block, preventing the TUI from processing input or closing overlays while a copy is in progress.

## What changed

- Route clipboard copies through one session worker that retains native clipboard ownership. Keep terminal escape output on the UI thread.
- Show pending and busy status messages, reject additional copies without queuing them, and ask users to retry image paste after an active copy finishes.
- Abandon setup after five seconds and prevent late delivery. Keep the worker busy until the blocked call returns, and bound shutdown waiting for clipboard handoff.
- Match completions to their originating requests so stale results cannot clear newer selections or unexpectedly resume transcript following. Retain selections on automatic copies, failures, and unconfirmed delivery.

## Testing

Add regression tests for blocked backends, overlay exit, copy and paste ordering, setup expiry, bounded shutdown, completion status messages, and preservation of replaced or moved selections.

prs.title: Preserve human overrides across repeated heartbeat instructions
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve human overrides across repeated heartbeat instructions

## Why

Unchanged scheduled heartbeat instructions should not become fresh authorization evidence that supersedes a later human override or floods Guardian review context.

## What changed

- Capture heartbeat provenance per input, including when steering an active turn, and persist it in history and retained context.
- Coalesce unchanged instructions for each automation at their original acceptance order. Preserve changed instruction versions and ordinary human messages.
- Represent repeated heartbeats as references to earlier instructions in Guardian transcripts, while tracking the latest input turn separately for trusted skill selection.
- Limit coalescing to recognized, bounded heartbeat envelopes with host-provided provenance.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for human overrides across repeated and steered heartbeats, instruction changes, checkpoint restoration, transcript references, envelope parsing, and latest-turn trusted skills in delegated reviews.

prs.title: Avoid blocking async proxy resolution on the system proxy cache
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Avoid blocking async proxy resolution on the system proxy cache

## Why

Platform proxy resolution holds the system proxy cache mutex, so checking the cache could block a Tokio worker while another lookup was in progress.

## What changed

Use `try_lock` for cache reads, treating contention as a cache miss so async callers on Windows and macOS wait through the existing asynchronous resolver path.

## Testing

Add a Windows/macOS regression test that verifies resolution yields while the cache is locked and completes after release. Adapt the cached-route test to tolerate concurrent cache writers, and isolate the unavailable-decision cache test from shared cache contention.

prs.title: Initialize media estimates outside the global cache lock
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Initialize media estimates outside the global cache lock

## Why

Image and audio estimate cache misses computed values while holding the cache mutex, blocking access to unrelated keys during initialization.

## What changed

Add `BlockingLruCache::get_or_init` using `Arc<OnceLock<V>>` and migrate the image and audio estimate caches to it. Initialization and same-key waits run in a Tokio blocking region after releasing the cache mutex. Callers share initialization while an entry remains cached; eviction can allow another initialization, so factories must be deterministic.

## Testing

Add a concurrency test covering access to other keys during initialization, eviction of an in-flight entry, and successful completion of both the evicted initializer and its replacement.

prs.title: Validate loaded plugins outside the cache lock
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Validate loaded plugins outside the cache lock

## Why

Checking installed plugin roots performs filesystem work while holding the loaded plugins cache mutex, blocking lookups for other cache keys.

## What changed

Store cache entries in `Arc`s and release the mutex before validating installation paths. After reacquiring the lock, check the cache generation and entry identity to reject entries invalidated or replaced during validation. Preserve stale-entry eviction and most-recently-used ordering.

prs.title: Avoid nested read locking when rendering browser sign-in
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Avoid nested read locking when rendering browser sign-in

## Why

`render_ref` already holds a read lock on `sign_in_state`. Acquiring another read lock in `render_continue_in_browser` can deadlock when a writer is waiting.

## What changed

Pass the borrowed `ContinueInBrowserState` from `render_ref` into the browser sign-in renderer instead of reading the lock again.

## Testing

Update the existing narrow-width browser sign-in test to exercise `render_ref`, retaining checks for the full OSC 8 authentication link, device-code guidance, and cancellation footer.

prs.title: Render remote permission paths using executor context
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Render remote permission paths using executor context

## What changed

- Resolve remote sandbox modes, writable roots, and denied read paths/globs using the executor's filesystem context, displaying paths in its native format. Preserve local filesystem resolution for local environments.
- Resolve remote read denials individually so missing executor facts omit only the unresolved entries.
- Apply a shared 32 KiB budget to displayed permission paths/globs, omitting whole entries and warning that all restrictions still apply, including omitted read denials.

## Testing

Add coverage for remote Windows writable roots and read denials, missing executor path facts, and whole-entry omission with multibyte paths under the shared budget.

prs.title: Add opt-in OTLP logging for Guardian assessments
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add opt-in OTLP logging for Guardian assessments

## What changed

Add `otel.log_guardian_assessments`, disabled by default and requiring an OTLP HTTP or gRPC log exporter. Emit `codex.guardian_assessment` when a synchronous Guardian review finishes, including review identifiers, status, risk level, user authorization, and rationale. Include `allow` or `deny` outcomes only for completed model assessments, not review errors, timeouts, or cancellations.

Cap exported rationales at 64 KiB on a UTF-8 character boundary and record their original byte length and truncation status. Use the log-only route to exclude assessment payloads from trace export, local state logs, and bug-report log buffers. Cached V2 approvals are not included.

## Testing

Add coverage for configuration gating, enabled and disabled denial logging, terminal statuses and outcomes, UTF-8 rationale truncation, export routing, and bug-report log buffer exclusion.

prs.title: Fix PID reservation test race and update guardian heartbeat snapshot
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix PID reservation test race and update guardian heartbeat snapshot

## Why

The PID reservation test could race with the backend's read on Windows by deleting the PID file from its cleanup task. The guardian heartbeat snapshot and environment normalization also needed to match the current permission-context wording.

## What changed

- Release the reservation lock and let `stop()` remove the stale PID file, then assert that the file is gone.
- Update the guardian heartbeat snapshot and normalization pattern to use `The active permission profile for environment`.

prs.title: Measure deferred tool namespace fragments before and after truncation
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Measure deferred tool namespace fragments before and after truncation

## What changed

Record `codex.thread.tools.namespaces_total` and `codex.thread.tools.fragment_bytes` histograms through session telemetry. Tag samples by `stage` (`before` or `after` the 4 KiB cap) and `kind` (`snapshot` or `delta`). Measure bytes after description normalization and XML escaping, including the `<tools>` wrapper, with explicit fragment-size buckets.

Delta counts include only changed entries, and unchanged state emits no samples.

## Testing

Extend rendering tests to verify snapshot and delta metrics, omission counts, byte sizes with Unicode and XML escaping, and no samples for unchanged state.

prs.title: Fix macOS system-alias matching in patch permission checks
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix macOS system-alias matching in patch permission checks

## Why

Local `apply_patch` permission checks can treat a macOS system alias and its canonical spelling as different locations, sending writes covered by temporary-directory grants for unnecessary approval.

## What changed

- Normalize trusted top-level aliases in local policy roots and patch targets, reusing a prepared matcher for permission requests and patch safety checks.
- Share alias normalization with Seatbelt and the macOS executor sandbox while preserving mutable symlinks and missing descendants.
- Preserve read-only and deny precedence, protected metadata restrictions, and remote URI matching. Propagate normalization failures from fallible permission checks.

## Testing

Add macOS regressions for multi-file patches with missing parent directories through both direct `apply_patch` calls and shell interception, asserting automatic approval and file contents. Add unit coverage for alias restriction precedence, mutable symlink preservation, missing descendants, and remote permission isolation.

prs.title: Use Tokio's clock for TUI paste timing
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Use Tokio's clock for TUI paste timing

## Why

Paste input classification and asynchronous flush deadlines need to share a clock, including when Tokio time is paused in tests.

## What changed

Use Tokio's clock for chat composer paste timing and startup draft newline tracking, converting to `std::time::Instant` where existing composer helpers require it.

## Testing

Run the existing startup draft multiline paste test with `start_paused = true`. It checks that non-bracketed pastes preserve newlines without submitting the draft.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix zsh alias quoting in sourced shell snapshots

## Why

Sourced snapshots parse options and aliases as a group before restored options take effect. Aliases serialized with `RC_QUOTES` enabled can therefore be misinterpreted by the replay shell.

## What changed

## Testing

Extend regression coverage to execute restored aliases with `RC_QUOTES` enabled and disabled across source and eval replay. Expand macOS zsh concurrent replay tests to cover quoted aliases, preserved options, and blocked descriptor paths with and without a TTY.

Local daemons use a remote request handle even though their login callback is local, so the TUI skipped opening the browser. Login completion could also arrive while the browser was opening, before the TUI had recorded the active login.

## What changed

Add regression tests for browser opening across embedded, local daemon, and remote targets, and for login completion during browser opening.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Centralize executable fixture creation to avoid Linux ETXTBSY races

## Why

Concurrent tests can inherit writable descriptors for executable fixtures, causing `ETXTBSY` when those fixtures launch on Linux.

## What changed

Expose shared `write_executable` and `copy_executable` helpers from `codex_utils_cargo_bin` and adopt them in CLI, exec-server, and MCP tests. On Linux, writes and copies complete in separate processes so sibling test spawns cannot inherit the writable descriptors. Script fixtures receive mode `0o755`, and copied executables retain their source permissions.

Remove the executable-busy retry loop from the program resolver test now that its script uses the shared helper.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix Unix socket connections through long symlink paths

## Why

An advertised control socket path can exceed the Unix socket path limit even when its symlink target is short enough to connect to.

## What changed

On Unix, resolve the socket path and retry the connection when the initial attempt returns `InvalidInput`.

## Testing

Add a regression test that creates control sockets under two long home paths, checks that their symlink targets are distinct, and verifies that clients can connect through both advertised paths.

prs.body:
Fix SGR mouse reporting for Windows terminal capture

## Why

Some Windows terminals send legacy mouse reports as key records. Requesting SGR reports lets ConPTY translate them into mouse records.

## What changed

Write and flush the SGR encoding request separately from `EnablePointerCapture`, so it also reaches terminals when capture uses the Windows console API. Explicitly reset SGR encoding during Windows mouse cleanup, even if restoring the console mode fails.

## Testing

Add regression tests for cleanup after SGR setup fails and an isolated Windows console test that checks mouse input activation, SGR encoding, and restoration of the original console mode and default encoding.
